text:
pagerduty: P1 incident: continuous-batcher nodes in us-west-2 exhibiting repeated OOMs, CUDA driver faults, and container restarts. auto-escalated to eng-oncall. incident_id=INC-20260315-02 :rotating_light:

mina: noticed p99 token latency shooting up from ~120ms to 6-12s around 2026-03-15T11:03:12Z. many requests returned 504. Error rate spike correlated with queue_depth and prefetch_bytes metrics.

aj: checking runtime dashboard — both cbatch pools show runaway batch sizes (some batches > 1024 tokens) and queue depth > 2k. KV cache miss rate also increased. suspect merge path bug in continuous-batcher.

sarah: pulled pod logs from gpu-node-7: repeated CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS, then oom_kill. snippet:
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
  what():  std::bad_alloc
E 0x7f9d3b4a cudaDriver: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
runtime::batch::merge_partial+0x6a
runtime::kv::entry_release+0x45
main+0xf3
```

kai: customer impact: dedicated customers C-5510 and C-5517 reported timeouts and degraded throughput. Support received ~8 high-severity tickets. ETA to stabilize estimated 45m after mitigations.

mina: immediate mitigation plan (live):
- throttle: set emergency max_batch_size=6 and queue_capacity=128 on affected pools
- flip off prefetch and aggressive kv caching (infra feature flag)
- rollback continuous-batcher to previous stable v1.13.4 where batching merge change didn't exist
- cordon and drain 3 flapping nodes, scale up extra replacement nodes to avoid capacity loss

aj: applying throttles now:
```
redwoodctl routes update --pool cbatch-gpu-west --max-batch-size 6 --queue-capacity 128
infractl feature-flag set cbatch.prefetch.enabled=false --scope pool:cbatch-gpu-*
deployctl rollback continuous-batcher --to v1.13.4 --region us-west-2
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7
kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

ops-bot: Rollback initiated: continuous-batcher 2026-03-15 v1.14.2 -> v1.13.4. Canary rollout in progress. :arrow_backward:

sarah: after throttles and rollback, new OOMs dropped sharply. p95 latency improved from 4.2s -> ~420ms within 6 minutes. still seeing two pods restart once each due to earlier corruption. saving logs to s3://redwood-logs/incidents/INC-20260315-02/ for postmortem.

aj: correlating stack traces — illegal address appears when merging batches that contain entries with prefetch-populated KV pointers. hypothesis: double-free or use-after-free when merge reassigns ownership during concurrent merge + eviction.

ryan: reprod attempt with stress harness (seq length dist + prefetch enabled) hit illegal address after ~900 iterations. adding extra refcounting guards and moving deferred free to GC queue. will open hotfix PR.

ops-bot: feature flag applied: cbatch.merge_single_thread=true on 2 canary nodes in us-west-2 for immediate safety. :white_check_mark:

kai: customer comms: initial notice sent to affected customers at 11:12 UTC. support is drafting timeline and remediation note.

mina: handoff notes for next oncall in 30m: incident currently stabilized under mitigations (prefetch disabled, max_batch_size=6, queue_capacity=128, rollback to v1.13.4). monitoring for residual restarts. followups: eng-runtime root cause, eng-sre validate autoscaler tolerance to cordon/drain, support collection of impacted request IDs.

ryan: PR #3281 opened with patch: add deferred_free_queue + guard on kv_entry lifetime; includes regression test running harness x20 iterations. https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/3281 :eyes:

aj: plan to canary patched v1.14.3 to single pool once PR passes: steps — keep prefetch disabled, enable merge_single_thread=false only after verifying no regresses. running perf to measure latency impact of deferred-free.

zara: taking over at 11:38 UTC. I'll keep watches for 2 hours and coordinate postmortem. please attach any additional logs and the customer impact spreadsheet to the incident ticket.

support: compiling affected customer list and request IDs. prepping templated apology + timeline for outbound comms.

sarah: metrics to capture for postmortem: OOMKill count per node, restart timestamps, p99 delta, number of affected requests, and rollback timing. uploading dashboards and raw logs to the incident bucket.

mina: final actions executed for live mitigation:
```
# emergency throttles
redwoodctl routes update --pool cbatch-gpu-west --max-batch-size 6 --queue-capacity 128
# disable prefetch
infractl feature-flag set cbatch.prefetch.enabled=false --scope pool:cbatch-gpu-*
# rollback
deployctl rollback continuous-batcher --to v1.13.4 --region us-west-2
# cordon/drain noisy nodes
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7 gpu-node-12 gpu-node-19
kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

ryan: will request canary deploy of v1.14.3 (hotfix) to pool cbatch-gpu-west-1 with prefetch initially off. if stable for 30m, re-enable prefetch per-pool incrementally.

zara: incident marked P1; owners assigned for follow-ups. postmortem due EOD with timeline, root cause, RCA, and customer impact. channel will stay open. :clipboard:
